newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares jump but fundamentals stay the same.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares jump but fundamentals stay the same.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange index rose nearly two percent on Wednesday in a surprise rally following a two-week tumble but analysts were cautious about the market's near-term direction.
The 30-share composite index leapt 56.14 points, or 1.92 percent, to close at 2,983.57 on institutional buying as well as some block sales.
"There was no fresh news that could have sparked the rally. Everything is technical at this point," Michelle Peneyra, research analyst at Citibank Securities, said.
She said stock prices, especially the index heavyweights and property stocks, had reached their perceived bottom, prompting bargain hunting despite the lack of market-moving news.
The composite index has fallen 242.35 points, or 7.64 percent, since the start of the month, closing at its seven-month low of 2,927.43 on Tuesday.
Frenzied buying in markets in Hong Kong and the United States had diverted the attention of foreign fund managers from the local bourse, brokers said.
Leading the freefall were property issues on fears the sector had peaked.
From the start of the month until Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange's property index had fallen 14.83 percent to 140.01 points.
The market was further dampened late last week after a sudden change in the Senate leadership.
"It's becoming clear that the president's economic agenda is not in trouble with the new Senate leadership," Joey Roxas, president of Eagle Equities, said.
But technicals still suggested the index could fall another 50 points before staging a convincing recovery, he said.
"As of now, the market hasn't broken the downtrend line," he added.
Raul Ruiz, vice president for research of Sun Hung Kai Securities, said it was too early to say if the market had turned the corner. "Fundamentals have not really changed," he said.
However some investors could have been accumulating selected issues in anticipation of third quarter earnings announcements, he said.

Citbank's Peneyra said the market already expected positive corporate results, thus any good news would have already been discounted, but pockets of exceptional net income figures might stir the market.
Rolando Pineda, vice president of Tower Securities, said the index could retest the 3,000 barrier in the coming days, but predicted that further consolidation might follow.
"We will be trading within a tight range," Pineda said, especially since politics has started to creep back into national consciousness as the 1998 presidential election nears.
